_comment: Every group of 2+ ref/method rows that legitimately share the exact same (analyte, sex, age, preg) key — found by Stage 2a's collision check. These are NOT classification errors: each row genuinely applies to the same coarse demographic bucket, distinguished only by a clinical condition the sex/age/preg chips don't express (a finer age band, menstrual-cycle phase, time of draw, specimen type, or another one-off covariate). bestRange() in shell.html used to pick one of these silently, by array order, whenever none scored higher than the others — the same class of silent-wrong-value risk as the original My Lab bug, just in the interpreter's row-picker instead of the override store. The fix: the Result Interpreter now detects a tie against this list and makes the user pick which row applies, by its own grp label, instead of guessing (see activeRange()/bestRange() and renderInterp() in shell.html). qa/validate_ties.js fails the build if a NEW, unlisted tie shows up among ref/method rows for any test — the same append-only-review discipline as qa/validate_rids.js, so a future content update can't silently reintroduce a guessed pick without a human looking at it first.

_dimension_summary.age-subband: A single age bucket (adult, neonate) is too coarse — the real reference interval changes within it (ESR by decade, IGF-1 by decade, testosterone by decade, PSA by decade, cystatin ≥60y, bilirubin by hours-of-life, ammonia preterm/sick-neonate).
_dimension_summary.cycle-phase: Reproductive hormones vary by menstrual-cycle phase or menopausal status, which the sex/age/preg chips don't capture (LH, FSH, estradiol, progesterone, 17-OHP, and bone turnover markers by meno status).
_dimension_summary.timing: Same analyte, same patient, different expected value depending on WHEN or under what test condition it's drawn (cortisol/ACTH by time of day, glucose random vs post-prandial).
_dimension_summary.one_off_covariate: A single extra covariate with no other home in the schema (lactate venous vs arterial specimen, vWF by ABO blood group, CEA by smoking status, Bence Jones ratio by renal function).

groups._why: Same already-reviewed age-subband tie as before (PSA reference range changes by decade) — key and rids changed only because assign_analyte_keys.py/retire_and_reassign.py gave every PSA row an explicit analyte.key to split off the free:total ratio (r11) and biochemical-recurrence threshold (r12), which were bundled under the old blank key.

_ladder_fallback_comment: Stage 2b gave every dx/cutoff/target row a `kind` and taught the interpreter to classify a value against them automatically when they form a clean, value-ordered ladder (classifyAgainstLadder()/isValueLadder() in shell.html) — e.g. Vitamin D's deficient/insufficient/sufficient/toxic bands need no prompt, the entered number picks one. A SMALL number of same-key dx/cutoff/target groups aren't a value ladder at all: picking between them needs clinical context a number can't supply (which drug, which indication, which dosing schedule). Those are listed here so a future content change that creates an unreviewed new one gets a human look, exactly like the ref/method list above — but unlike that list, the interpreter does NOT block on these: it shows the raw value plus an informational note naming the candidates, because none of them can be silently mis-picked (there is no single verdict being guessed at) — it simply can't go further without the clinician's own judgement.

ladder_fallback_groups._why: INR therapeutic target depends on WHY the patient is anticoagulated (AF/VTE/tissue valve vs. a mechanical mitral valve), not on the INR number itself.
Anti-Xa target depends on the drug/regimen (LMWH prophylaxis vs. treatment once- or twice-daily vs. unfractionated heparin), not on the level itself.
Digoxin's target band depends on the indication (heart failure vs. atrial fibrillation) as well as the level; the two targets overlap rather than forming a clean ladder.

Found by qa/test5.py — the age-adjusted cutoff (r2, 'age × 10') has no fixed numeric bound at all, only a formula, so it can never be placed on a value ladder; the interpreter correctly falls back to naming both cutoffs rather than silently applying the <50y one to an older patient.

r2 (Prediabetes 5.7-6.4) and r3 (Diabetes >=6.5) alone would form a clean 2-band ladder for classifying a fresh reading, but r4 ('General treatment target', <7.0, individualise) is a different axis entirely — a treatment goal for someone already diagnosed, not a diagnostic band for a fresh number — and has no fixed numeric bound (text-only), so it can't be placed on the same ladder. Correctly falls back rather than silently grading an already-diagnosed patient's treatment-target check against the diagnostic bands.

r2/r3/r4 are age-banded acute 'rule in' cutoffs (needs the patient's age, like ESR's age-subband pattern) and r5 (acute rule-out, <300 pg/mL) is text-only with no fixed numeric bound, while r1 is a separate non-acute 'unlikely' cutoff — the group mixes an age dimension with a non-numeric row and can never form one clean value ladder. Correctly falls back to naming the candidates; picking the right one needs the patient's age and whether the presentation is acute, not just the number.

ANA is reported as a titre (<1:80, 1:80, 1:160, >=1:320), not a plain number, so none of its rows carry a numeric lo/hi at all — they can never form a value ladder. The Result Interpreter's numeric-value entry isn't the right tool for a titre test in the first place; this is a harmless, inherent mismatch rather than a data error.

Trisomy 21 screen-negative/positive results are reported as a risk ratio ('1 in 250'), not a plain number, so neither row carries a numeric lo/hi — they can never form a value ladder. Same inherent text-only mismatch as ANA's titre rows.
